_comment: Example vibe.config.json — the only project-specific file the tooling reads (scripts/lib/vibe-config.mjs). Let init-project.mjs write a real one, or copy this and edit it. JSON has no comments, so every note lives in a _comment key instead; nothing reads those keys. Only "slug" is required: loadConfig() merges this file over its built-in defaults, so a half-filled config still runs and the scripts report what is missing rather than failing deep inside a later step. Paths are absolute, or relative to <root>.
_comment_top: identity of the film. slug names the HyperFrames project folder videos/<slug> and is the one required key. track is the music file as delivered by the user, relative to <root> (null if the film ships without music). fps/width/height are the canvas every frame is authored against — band rows below are in these pixels. language/platforms drive the publishing assets.

bands._comment: the reserved vertical bands, in canvas pixels — the film's layout law (references/03-design-system.md). audit-still.mjs measures ink and edge energy per row; frame-openings.mjs asserts subtitle ink in [subtitle[0], subtitle[1]]. Change these only if you change the canvas.

cue._comment: subtitle legality gates (sync-storyboard-timings.mjs). maxCharsPerSecond is the reading-speed ceiling for Chinese copy; a cue shorter than minSeconds, or closer than minGapSeconds to its neighbour, is rejected rather than silently rendered.

timing._comment: verification tolerances (verify-timing.mjs). Every cut and cue must land within toleranceMs of the fitted grid; the rendered audio is then re-measured acoustically with the per-role windows below.

acousticToleranceMs._comment: a hit is judged at its attack, a whoosh at its midpoint, a riser at its end, so the acoustic windows are wider than the grid tolerance.

sound._comment: mix defaults (mix-soundtrack.mjs): bgmGainDb is applied to the music, sfxTrimDb lifts the sfx stem, and the finished mix is checked against targetLufs — bilibili normalises towards -14 LUFS.

_comment_fonts: the faces build-fonts.mjs subsets and inject-fonts.mjs inlines. file must name a real font FILE on this machine, because the script subsets it: a named family with no in-file @font-face is rejected by lint, and HyperFrames' alias table has no CJK entry at all. css is the family name the CSS refers to, role is which text register the face serves, and axes is optional — when present it is passed to subset-font as variationAxes, which pins a variable font to one instance (omit it for a static font). init-project.mjs probes the machine's font registry and also records "family" for readability; nothing reads that key. The paths below are placeholders — replace every one of them.
_comment_charsetExtra: characters to include in the font subset even though no source file contains them yet — a margin so a small copy edit does not force a font rebuild. build-fonts.mjs harvests a charset from STORYBOARD.md, BRIEF.md, frame.md, every data/*.json and audio/cue-map.json, then appends this string. The value below is the reference film's Chinese margin (its own vocabulary plus the words a revision is likely to introduce); replace it with your own, and keep the digits, Latin and punctuation, which cost almost nothing.

_comment_lifeWindows: the windows a computed figure is allowed to talk about (compute-life-window.mjs): the observation phase ends at from + (1/e) x (to - from). A window is the viewer's own input, not a fact, and the film has to say so on screen. The three below are the reference film's; compute-life-window.mjs falls back to exactly this list when the key is absent. Replace them — and see compute-optimal-stopping.mjs, which is the other worked example of the rule that every figure is computed, never invented.
